name: Nehemiah
bio: Nehemiah son of Hachaliah served as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes of Persia at the palace in Susa. In the twentieth year of the king's reign, his brother Hanani and other men arrived from Judah and told him that the Jewish remnant there lived in great trouble and disgrace, with Jerusalem's wall broken down and its gates burned. Nehemiah wept, mourned, and fasted for days, praying to the LORD and confessing Israel's sins, and asking God to grant him success and favor before the king as he prepared to make a request of him (Nehemiah 1:1-11). His own leadership in rebuilding Jerusalem's wall is told in detail in the chapters ahead.  When King Artaxerxes noticed Nehemiah's sorrow, Nehemiah explained his grief over Jerusalem's ruin and, after praying silently, asked to be sent there to rebuild it; the king granted his request, set him a timeframe, and gave him letters of safe passage and a supply of timber, along with an armed escort. Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official were furious to hear a man had come seeking Israel's welfare. After three days in Jerusalem, Nehemiah secretly surveyed the broken walls and burned gates by night before telling anyone his plan. He then rallied the Jews, priests, and nobles to rebuild the wall, telling them of God's favor and the king's support; they agreed at once. When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab mocked them as rebels against the king, Nehemiah answered that God would give them success and that these men had no share, right, or claim in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:1-20).
